value: BOUNDARY AND CORRECTION on claim.law.NC_pre-frame-addr16-lo-into-r0-owes-a-callee-saved-copy.20260903.v1. That law's PROLOGUE CLASS is real and its r0 half is unchallenged: where ours completes an ADDR16_LO before the frame-opening `stwu` INTO r0, a later copy is owed. Its DISCRIMINATOR, however, does not hold in the direction it is stated. The law says the split is clean -- 'FOUR write it into r0 and every one of those owes the mr ... SEVEN write it into a NAMED volatile and none of them owes a copy, because those values are consumed as call arguments or temps rather than parked in a web' -- and game/enemy/critter::ProcessCritterList is a TWELFTH pre-frame instance that writes into a NAMED VOLATILE AND OWES A COPY. MEASURED at commit 47ae4d37c on the live bytes, `python tools/gdl/fnasm.py game/enemy/critter ProcessCritterList 0x0:0x60 --diff`: ours emits `@0x04 lis r4,0 @gPlayers(ADDR16_HA)`, then `@0x10 addi r4,r4,0 @gPlayers(ADDR16_LO)` -- destination r4, a named volatile, NOT r0, and BEFORE the frame-opening `@0x18 stwu r1,-24(r1)` -- and then pays `@0x1c addi r5,r4,0`, a surplus copy into the loop's induction register. The target spends one instruction where ours spends two: `@0x04 lis r3,0 @gPlayers(ADDR16_HA)` then `@0x1c addi r5,r3,0 @gPlayers(ADDR16_LO)`, written FRESH into r5, freeing r3 for the byte-offset induction variable at `@0x24 addi r3,r6,0`. The counts are 50/49 (ours/target). THIS IS ONE OF THE PARENT LAW'S OWN NAMED FALSIFIERS, discharged verbatim: 'a re-run of the census below in which the r0-versus-named-volatile discriminator fails to separate the two groups'. WHY THE PARENT MISSED IT, and this is the transferable part: the parent's census covered 36 functions in 15 TUs and its own closing sentence says the population 'is a floor over 36 screened functions and not an image-wide total'. game/enemy/critter was not in it. A discriminator derived from a floor is a hypothesis about the floor, and the parent was careful enough to say so -- the error is in reading its two-group split as settled, not in the law's authorship. TWO CONSEQUENCES. (1) The copy is owed by something OTHER than the destination being r0 specifically; ProcessCritterList's copy destination is volatile r5 and its source r4 is volatile too, so `parked in a web` versus `consumed as a call argument` is the surviving candidate distinction and the register identity is not. (2) A SECOND-ORDER PREDICTION OF THE PARENT SURVIVES AND IS CONFIRMED HERE: the parent reports that declaration order is 'CATEGORICALLY DEAD ON A MEMBER' and that the only source lever measured to move such a prologue is a CROSS-CLASS declaration exchange between locals of different construct classes. ProcessCritterList has exactly one address-class local and three int-class locals, so no such exchange exists, and three declaration orders measured on it in run 54 all left the surplus copy and the 50/49 count untouched (attempt.CR_processcritterlist-the-declaration-order-lever-is-inert-here-so-the-addr16lo-reachable-remainder-is-zero.20260904.v1). The parent's disposition for a member -- do not spend probes on declaration order, declaration form, or opt_propagation -- therefore stands and is strengthened by an instance it did not know about.
